bug_semantics: Rainbond region API broken access control / cross-enterprise IDOR (CWE-639). Tenants are enterprise-scoped (Tenants.EID) and region API tokens are issued per enterprise (RegionUserInfo.EID), but CheckToken only tests expiry and a coarse APIRange/Range class (ALLPOWER/SERVERSOURCE/NODEMANAGER) and never reads regionInfo.EID. FullToken therefore accepts any still-valid enterprise token. InitTenant then resolves chi URL param tenant_name via GetTenantIDByName (global WHERE name = ?), with no comparison to the caller's EID, so one enterprise's token can GET/PUT/DELETE another enterprise's /v2/tenants/{tenant_name}/... services, plugins, env vars, and certificates. Researcher PoC on v3.6.1 and retest on v6.9.7 both returned another tenant's service list with HTTP 200.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable mechanism was first written in b9981602508f599126b7d90122eefcb7756f8fc5 (2017-12-03, 崔斌 <cuiminmm@gmail.com>, '[ADD]Add user token Dispatcher and token verify'). That single-parent commit introduced RegionUserInfo with an EID column, TokenDispatcher that persists tokens keyed by EID ('token包含 eid，数据中心标识，可控范围，有效期'), CheckToken that authorizes solely on ValidityPeriod plus Range, and FullToken that gates the API through CheckToken. The parent already had Tenants.EID and InitTenant's unscoped name lookup; those are preconditions, not the BIC. Later CheckToken edits (cache fallback, APIRange rename, gofmt) never added an EID comparison. The 2017 human first-write is the BIC; the 2026 Codex-branch fix is out of scope for AI attribution.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-72741 is a live published VulnCheck record (not withdrawn or rejected), matching GHSA-5xhp-2v8r-m7wh and issue #2665. The bug is missing authorization on a per-enterprise token: tokens and tenants both carry EID, but the gate that accepts the token never binds those EIDs, and tenant_name in the URL is a global key. That is a real CWE-639 through 6.9.7, closed in 6.9.8 by deleting the legacy token class rather than adding an EID check. BIC search used git log -L on CheckToken at v6.9.7, not an AI-commit hunt. The smallest first-write of the flawed gate is b9981602, which also created the EID-bearing token model; the immediate parent lacks those objects and still has only a single cluster TOKEN plus unscoped InitTenant. Subsequent CheckToken commits are cache/range refactors that do not introduce the missing comparison, so they are not BICs. Tag order matches the advisory: BIC precedes v3.6.1 and v6.9.7; the PR #2674 patch is not in v6.9.7 and is in v6.9.8. AI judgment is BIC-only: 2017 human author/committer 崔斌, empty trailer set. The later Codex branch that removed the tokens is the fix, so it cannot attribute the introducer. Closed NOT_AI with proven BIC and landed fix.
